ABSTRACT: Flexibility and demand-response programmes check the performance of each enrolled building in each settlement period, so day-ahead load intervals must be reliable building by building and week by week, from the first days after metering starts. Conformal intervals pooled over other buildings are calibrated only on average. We propose two-timescale shrinkage conformal calibration (TTSC): a slow component shrinks the score distribution of previously onboarded buildings towards the new building's recency-weighted own scores, and a fast component corrects the building's miscoverage level from its misses in the last seven days. Both parameters are selected by leave-one-building-out for weekly reliability. On 1,042 buildings (Building Data Genome 2) and 316 Portuguese electricity clients, compared with pooled, online, temporal, hierarchical and shrinkage calibration on the same forecasts, pooled conformalised quantile regression left 23.7% and 18.4% of new buildings under-covered in a typical week. TTSC reduced this to 13.6% and 6.7%, below the 17.3% and 12.8% that perfectly calibrated static intervals would show, and buildings with any week below 0.80 from 51.2% to 20.0% (BDG2), at a median interval score about 2–3 % higher. Neither timescale alone achieved this. Results held on runs held out from the method's design, unseen sites, cross-country transfer and fourteen stress tests. In weekly-settled capacity-headroom offers, TTSC reduced failed weekly performance checks from 17.5% to 14.1% of building-weeks at similar average cost and negligible computational cost.
